summary: A remembered claim now has a size limit, and a claim can span more than one message.
details: The subject and object of a remembered fact had no length limit at all, and the subject is the key everything else looks it up by. Both now cap at a configurable length, with a hard limit underneath that config cannot exceed, and lowering the limit below claims already stored stops Nora starting and names them rather than silently shortening what someone said.

A claim can be made across several messages — someone starting a sentence and finishing it — so Nora now records every message a claim came from instead of picking one. A claim attributed to a message that was not in front of her is discarded whole rather than trimmed.

A new check compares what Nora asks a background model to return against what her code actually reads, so a field on one side only fails the build instead of producing a subsystem that runs cleanly and remembers nothing.
limitations: Objects longer than 200 characters are now discarded at extraction. Anything that long is a sentence rather than a thing, and the promotion rule already refused it.
